summary: Malheur refuge tower built by the CCC in 1933 near the original P Ranch; closed at its base for wildlife, viewable from the road.

facts.design: 72-foot steel Aermotor tower with a 7 by 7 foot metal cab
facts.agency: U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service, Malheur National Wildlife Refuge

access.note: Closed to public access most of the year for bird nesting habitat (register). The area around the base was closed due to wildlife in April 2024. Tower remains available for emergency use.

visit.trail_note: View from the road, the parking lot or the Riverview trail; reached from Frenchglen by the Steens Mountain Loop and Center Patrol Road, following the P-Ranch signs (April 2024 visit)

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps near the site of the original P Ranch
The site became part of the adjacent Wildlife Refuge
The main P Ranch house burned (the ranch house, not the lookout)
Registered July 16, 2002; nominated by Howard Verschoor
Visit May 15, 2012: lowest stairs overgrown, tower apparently unused; site listed it as abandoned
Visit April 2024: tower standing; base area closed due to wildlife; turkey vultures roosting on it

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Cheryl Hill's 2012 visit listed the tower as abandoned, with overgrown stairs. The register says it remains available for emergency use, and the April 2024 visit found it standing with its base closed to visitors. Standing is taken as current.

sources.title: Lookout Towers of the Malheur National Wildlife Refuge

notes_for_editor: Build year (1933), tower height (72 ft) and CCC origin agree across the register, firelookout.com and the 2024 blog. Purpose is unresolved: firelookout.com says it was primarily for wildlife observation; Cheryl Hill doubts it was used for fire detection. Current status and access rest on an April 2024 blog visit and the register's undated text; nothing newer was found. The 2024 blog's tower-height conflict (80/90/99 ft) concerns a different refuge tower (the headquarters tower, US 429), not this one. Wikipedia's P Ranch article (NRHP 1979) describes the ranch and was read but not used for the lookout. The fws.gov Malheur cultural heritage page appeared in search and was not read.
